title: Potato Salad with Light Mayonnaise Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad made with a light mayonnaise-type dressing is a classic dish where boiled potatoes are tossed with a gentle, low‑fat mayo‑based sauce. It is popular as a side dish or a light meal, especially during warm weather.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In many countries the salad is a staple at picnics and family gatherings.
Light mayonnaise dressing contains fewer fats and calories than regular mayo, often using reduced‑fat oil or yogurt.
The salad is commonly garnished with fresh herbs such as dill or parsley and finely chopped onion.
Some regional variations add boiled eggs, pickles, or a touch of mustard for extra flavor.
Potato salad keeps well in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide slowly digestible carbs that supply steady energy and help maintain blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The salad retains vitamin B6 and folate, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, a mineral that aids blood‑pressure regulation and heart health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using a light mayo reduces saturated fat content, making the dish more suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: If the potato skins are left on, the salad adds dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Traditional mayo contains eggs; people with egg allergy should use an egg‑free alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Excess salt in the dressing can raise blood pressure; monitor added salt.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: Leaving the salad at room temperature for more than 2 hours can allow bacterial proliferation.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even a light dressing adds calories; portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a side to meat, fish, or as a light standalone meal. Garnish with herbs, sliced boiled eggs, or olives for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Consume within 3‑4 days. Stir before serving as the dressing may settle.
